[Rating: 1/10] Update: Down to a 1. This an egregiously horrible design.   This game angers me more each time I play it. It is so so bad, and it has no reason to be. It is utterly devoid of [i]design[/i]  My deckbuilding-loving 11-year-old put it best when he declared that “This game isn’t fun if you try to win”  That’s an accurate, and damning, indictment. The game doesn’t suit its goal. It’s mucking about for mucking about’s sake.    There’s an entire subset of action cards that just draws cards from your or opponent’s decks then immediately return them.   That’s not because there’s some hugely important t

[Rating: 1/10] I think I gave it enough chances, but it's quite possibly the most frustrating game I've ever played. Building a deck and trashing the same cards you bought just doesn't make for a good game. Instead, it becomes a numbers game with some secondary abilities that you activate from time to time. The game mechanics contradict each other so much that it's no fun at all.

[Rating: 2/10] Pretty much the opposite of fun in a game to me. There's no control, just luck and chaos, not even anything new.  Not even the nice squirrels can save this game...

[Rating: 2/10] I was part of a demo at this year's Origins.  Like a film, I can usually tell in the first few minutes if I will like a game or not.  And like a film despite the twist and turns it may take, I've found that to be a pretty accurate statement for my game-playing and movie-watching history.  I was tuned out after two rounds and didn't find much fun in Dale of Merchants.  You have different animal card sets, but ultimately everyone is playing all the animals anyway.  Meh.  Not a game I liked.  Make it more asymmetrical and then we're talking.

[Rating: 2/10] I was liking the concept at first, then the fact we have to literally memorize what cards are in the deck more than enjoying the different effects soiled completely the game for me. Pretty disappointed by this one.

[Rating: 2/10] Possibly the most pointless and annoying deck builder ever made. I like building a deck if cards in order to accomplish something with them. In this game, you collect new cards in order to lay them down in a tableau. Put another way, you collect cards in order to show that you have them. Perfectly anti-climatic.

[Rating: 2/10] How do people like this?! This game takes everything good about Dominion and ruins it by introducing direct player targeting.  It's literally full of chaos for the sake of chaos. I can't remember have less fun with a game, and it took 2 hours nonetheless. You spend just as much time reading cards as you do actually playing the game.  If you like thinking about decisions that hardly matter at all, you might like this game!

[Rating: 3/10] Interesting UNDERDEVELOPED idea.  The cards are all too powerful and after buying a couple of cheap ones to use their powers, the other cards ore nothing but numbers you need to win the game.  If the game had two types of cards:   - action cards you use to perform actions / buy  - goods card that can only be used to build your stall  it would work much better.

[Rating: 3/10] Way too much text to read on every single card. Every deck has cards that contain a large paragraph of text that make you read the equivalent of a small pamphlet whenever its your turn. If you don't bother to read all this text on other players turns you end up not knowing what they are doing or how to react to it.  There is a deck of card that adds randomness without providing any level of fun.

[Rating: 3/10] This was utterly dull: a simple race to 8 ... and if you try to use your species' power, you just fall behind and lose. Can't see us ever giving this another try.  Maybe deckbuilders just aren't for us?

[Rating: 3/10] Nothing interesting in this game for me. I felt like the actions on the cards are not giving anything.  Sold 2020.04.07

[Rating: 3/10] Played a few times with my husband. I don't know... I found it kinda boring. Maybe it would be better with more players - perhaps younger cousins or older aunts - as a more family friendly kind of game.
